detailed_analysis: The spectrum is a clean carbonate Raman fingerprint on a low, slightly negative-slope baseline (minimal fluorescence). Band assignment: nu1 symmetric CO3 stretch at 1084.99 +/- 0.008 cm-1 (dominant, relative intensity 1.0, FWHM ~3 cm-1, high Lorentzian eta~0.8) with a co-located broad pedestal (~1082.6, FWHM 8, area ~20500); nu4 in-plane bend resolved as a doublet at 701.23 +/- 0.11 and 705.58 +/- 0.12 cm-1; lattice/external modes at 156, 188, 190, 213.4 +/- 0.15, 272.0, 283.7 cm-1; a weak satellite/wing at ~1110 cm-1; and a high-wavenumber pair at 1206.3 and 1238.3 cm-1 (nu1+lattice combination region). The diagnostic evidence for ARAGONITE over calcite is decisive: (1) the resolved nu4 doublet near 701/705 (calcite gives a single ~712 band), and (2) the strong lattice mode at ~213 cm-1 with a mode near ~156 (aragonite lattice pattern 152/206 vs calcite 156/282). The nu1 position of 1085.0 also sits at aragonite (1085) rather than calcite (1086) or dolomite (1097). Strong-band parameters are exceptionally well constrained (nu1 center to +/-0.008 cm-1). Weak lattice modes are poorly constrained: several eta values pin to 0 or bounds with uncertainties larger than the values, and peak_1 amplitude (96 +/- 67) and peak_2 amplitude (441 +/- 391) are barely significant. The nu1 core/base amplitude split is partially degenerate (base amplitude 2407 +/- 688). The persistent dispersive residual at the nu1 apex is physically meaningful: it suggests the real band is asymmetric, consistent with either instrumental/crystal-orientation effects or a genuine skewed lineshape not captured by symmetric pseudo-Voigts.

scientific_claims.claim: The spectrum is aragonite (CaCO3), identified by the resolved nu4 in-plane bend doublet at 701.23 +/- 0.11 and 705.58 +/- 0.12 cm-1, the nu1 symmetric stretch at 1084.99 +/- 0.008 cm-1, and lattice modes at 213.4 +/- 0.15 and ~156 cm-1 - a pattern that separates aragonite from calcite (single nu4 ~712, lattice ~282).
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Polymorph discrimination of CaCO3 by Raman is important for biomineralization, paleoclimate/diagenesis, and carbon sequestration studies, where aragonite-vs-calcite identification indicates formation conditions and stability. The resolved nu4 doublet provides an unambiguous, non-destructive polymorph marker.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone confirmed that the resolved ~701/705 cm-1 nu4 doublet together with the ~156/213 cm-1 lattice modes uniquely distinguishes aragonite from calcite in Raman spectra across sample environments?

model_type: Linear baseline + sum of 13 pseudo-Voigt components (nu1 core+base split; nu4 doublet resolved)

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline. Ten components: (1) ~150 cm⁻¹ weak lattice mode, (2) ~190 cm⁻¹ lattice/translational mode, (3) ~215 cm⁻¹ lattice/librational mode, (4) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (5) ~285 cm⁻¹ (resolved doublet), (6) ~702 cm⁻¹ and (7) ~706 cm⁻¹ (ν4 in-plane bend doublet), (8) ~1088 cm⁻¹ dominant ν1 symmetric stretch (sharp, high Lorentzian character), (9) ~1105 cm⁻¹ weak satellite/shoulder, (10) ~1210 cm⁻¹ and (11) ~1240 cm⁻¹ high-wavenumber pair. Model = linear baseline + Σ pseudo-Voigt.

issues.problem: The dominant peak is under-resolved: the fit undershoots the true maximum (data ≈22000 vs fit ≈21000) and cannot follow the sharp core, producing a large derivative-like (dispersive) residual with 4 sign-changes.
Systematic under-resolution: a real narrow feature near x≈142 and a small bump near x≈161 are not captured; the fit runs as a smooth curve missing these maxima.
Coherent oscillatory residual around the 213 peak indicating a lineshape/width mismatch on the leading edge.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Re-seed/retune components within the locked model: narrow peak_8 (eta more Lorentzian) at x≈1085 to remove the derivative residual and undershoot; re-seed peak_1 to x≈142 (narrower) and cover the ~161 shoulder; retune peak_3 width/eta near x≈213.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of eleven pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline (model structure unchanged/locked). Components: (1) ~142 cm⁻¹ weak sharp lattice mode (re-seeded from 150 to 142, narrower FWHM to catch the sharp low-x maximum), (2) ~190 cm⁻¹ lattice/translational mode, (3) ~213 cm⁻¹ lattice/librational mode (center/width/eta retuned to track the leading edge), (4) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (5) ~285 cm⁻¹ resolved doublet, (6) ~702 cm⁻¹ and (7) ~706 cm⁻¹ ν4 in-plane bend doublet, (8) ~1085 cm⁻¹ dominant ν1 symmetric stretch (re-seeded narrower with eta floated toward high Lorentzian character to capture the sharp core and remove the undershoot), (9) ~1105 cm⁻¹ weak satellite/shoulder, (10) ~1210 cm⁻¹ and (11) ~1240 cm⁻¹ high-wavenumber pair. The ~161 cm⁻¹ shoulder and the sharp/broad character of the 1085 band are represented by re-purposing/re-seeding existing nearby component slots rather than adding new profiles. Model = linear baseline + Σ pseudo-Voigt.

issues.problem: A clearly real data maximum at x≈190 (data ≈1100) is not captured; the fit runs at ≈600 through it. peak_2 (center 183, FWHM=22) is too broad and centered too low to reproduce this distinct feature.
Dominant peak remains under-resolved: fit undershoots the maximum (data ≈22000 vs fit ≈20500) and the core is slightly offset, producing a dispersive residual.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add a narrow pseudo-Voigt component seeded at x≈190 to capture the missed maximum, and narrow/increase-eta on peak_8 (x≈1085) to remove its dispersive residual.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of eleven pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline (model structure unchanged/locked; eleven components total). Components: (1) ~142 cm⁻¹ weak sharp lattice mode (narrow FWHM for the sharp low-x maximum), (2) ~183 cm⁻¹ broad lattice/translational base (kept broad, ~22 cm⁻¹, to represent the underlying base only), (3) re-purposed to ~190 cm⁻¹ narrow lattice/librational mode (re-seeded from ~213 to ~190 with narrow FWHM ~10 cm⁻¹ to resolve the distinct real maximum at x≈190, data ≈1100), with the ~213 leading-edge coverage folded into the retuned neighbor slots, (4) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (5) ~285 cm⁻¹ resolved doublet, (6) ~702 cm⁻¹ and (7) ~706 cm⁻¹ ν4 in-plane bend doublet, (8) ~1085 cm⁻¹ dominant ν1 symmetric stretch (narrow FWHM near lower physical bound, eta floated strongly toward Lorentzian η→1, center freed ±5 cm⁻¹ to follow the sharp core and remove the dispersive residual/undershoot), (9) ~1105 cm⁻¹ weak satellite/shoulder (may serve as the broad base under the ν1 core), (10) ~1210 cm⁻¹ and (11) ~1240 cm⁻¹ high-wavenumber pair. Model = linear baseline + Σ pseudo-Voigt. The ~161 cm⁻¹ shoulder and sharp/broad ν1 split continue to be represented by re-purposing existing nearby slots rather than adding profiles.

issues.problem: A prominent, strong real peak (data ≈1900 counts) is completely unmodeled; the fit runs nearly flat (~100) through it.
Dominant peak core under-resolved; fit undershoots the maximum and produces a dispersive residual.
Small real bump near x≈161 not captured.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Restore/seed a pseudo-Voigt component at x≈213 to recover the lost strong peak, and narrow peak_8 (higher Lorentzian eta) at x≈1085 to remove the dispersive core residual.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of eleven pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline (model structure locked; eleven components total). Component reassignment corrects the prior misallocation that left the strong x≈213 peak unmodeled and starved the low-x/ν1 regions: (1) ~161 cm⁻¹ narrow shoulder mode (RE-PURPOSED from the spurious, poorly constrained ~142 slot; seed narrow FWHM ~8–12 cm⁻¹ to capture the small real bump near 161), (2) ~183 cm⁻¹ broad lattice/translational base (kept broad, ~20–25 cm⁻¹, representing the underlying base only; not allowed to migrate to 190), (3) ~190 cm⁻¹ narrow lattice/librational mode (narrow FWHM ~8–12 cm⁻¹, center 190±5, resolving the distinct real maximum at data ≈1100), (4) ~213 cm⁻¹ strong lattice/librational mode (RE-SEEDED to recover the prominent real peak, data ≈1900 counts, that was completely unmodeled; narrow FWHM ~8–12 cm⁻¹), (5) ~272/285 cm⁻¹ resolved doublet consolidated into one of the mid-region slots, (6) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (7) ~285 cm⁻¹ resolved doublet, (8) ~1085 cm⁻¹ dominant ν1 symmetric stretch (narrow FWHM near lower bound ~2–4 cm⁻¹, eta floated strongly toward Lorentzian η→0.8–1.0, center freed ±5 cm⁻¹ to resolve the sharp core and remove the dispersive/undershoot residual), (9) ~1105 cm⁻¹ weak satellite/broad base beneath the ν1 core, (10) ~702/706 cm⁻¹ ν4 in-plane bend doublet, (11) ~1210/1240 cm⁻¹ high-wavenumber pair. Model = linear baseline + Σ pseudo-Voigt. Note: with eleven fixed slots, restoring 161, 190, and 213 while retaining 183 requires that the ν4 (702/706) and high-wavenumber (1210/1240) pairs each be represented by a single component (or that the 272/285 doublet share slots) — allocate slots to the strongest verified real features (161, 183, 190, 213, 272/285, 702, 1085, 1105, 1210, 1240) and drop the redundant/spurious former ~142 slot.

issues.problem: Dominant peak core under-resolved: fit peaks at ~21000 vs data ~22000, with a dispersive 4-sign-change residual (RMS/noise=197×). A single pseudo-Voigt cannot simultaneously match the sharp Lorentzian core and the broader base.
The ν4 doublet is modelled by a single asymmetric peak, leaving a dispersive residual (RMS/noise≈27–34, sign-changes on both edges).

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add a narrow high-Lorentzian core + broad base pair at ~1085 (split the ν1 slot rather than just narrowing it), and add the second ν4 doublet component at ~706 — structurally different fixes than the narrowing/re-seeding already tried.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline. The model is expanded from eleven to thirteen components to resolve two verified band-shape deficiencies that cannot be fixed at the parameter level. Component list: (1) ~161 cm⁻¹ narrow shoulder mode (FWHM ~8–12 cm⁻¹); (2) ~183 cm⁻¹ broad lattice/translational base (FWHM ~20–25 cm⁻¹, held broad, not allowed to migrate to 190/213); (3) ~190 cm⁻¹ narrow lattice/librational mode (FWHM ~8–12 cm⁻¹, amplitude to reach data ≈1100); (4) ~213 cm⁻¹ strong lattice/librational mode (FWHM ~8–12 cm⁻¹, amplitude to reach data ≈1900); (5) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (6) ~285 cm⁻¹ resolved doublet; (7) ~702 cm⁻¹ ν4 in-plane bend (first doublet member); (8) ~706 cm⁻¹ ν4 in-plane bend (SECOND doublet member, NEWLY ADDED — resolves the dispersive residual left by a single asymmetric peak; narrow FWHM ~4–10 cm⁻¹); (9) ~1085 cm⁻¹ ν1 symmetric-stretch CORE (very narrow FWHM near lower bound ~2–4 cm⁻¹, eta→0.8–1.0 Lorentzian, amplitude to reach data max ≈22000); (10) ~1085–1088 cm⁻¹ ν1 BASE (NEWLY ADDED co-located broader, lower-amplitude component, FWHM ~8–20 cm⁻¹, eta lower/more Gaussian — captures the broad pedestal that a single Voigt cannot fit simultaneously with the sharp core); (11) ~1105 cm⁻¹ weak satellite; (12) ~1210 cm⁻¹ and (13) ~1240 cm⁻¹ high-wavenumber pair. Model = linear baseline + Σ pseudo-Voigt. Rationale for structural change: (a) the ν1 core+base split is necessary because a single pseudo-Voigt has one shape parameter (eta) and cannot represent both a sharp Lorentzian core AND a broader pedestal — the 4-sign-change dispersive residual (RMS/noise=197×) is the signature of a shape mismatch, not a parameter mismatch, so narrowing alone (already tried, failed) cannot resolve it; (b) the ν4 doublet is physically two modes (~702/~706), so a single asymmetric peak produces dispersive edge residuals — a second component is the minimal correct fix.

issues.problem: Residual dispersive structure at the apex of the dominant peak (data ~22000 vs fit ~20000)
Fit slightly undershoots the wing/baseline shoulder

anchor_judge.reasoning: Candidate 1 achieves higher R² (0.9897 vs 0.9837) with a physically sound linear baseline and correctly resolves real spectral structure that Candidate 0 misses. The ~700-710 doublet (nu4) and the 1085 core+base split are clearly two overlapping components in the data, and Candidate 1 resolves them cleanly (see zoom panels), whereas Candidate 0 leaves systematic residual at 700 and misses the shoulder. Both show the characteristic derivative-shaped residual at the dominant ~1085 peak (unavoidable given the sharp intense line), but Candidate 1's overall residuals are flatter and less structured. Critically, Candidate 0's retuned ALS baseline is physically questionable in the 190 and 1180-1271 regions: its dashed baseline arches up under the 1200/1240 doublet, absorbing real peak intensity into the baseline and mis-modeling the low-frequency shoulder near 140-160 (visible in the zoom, where data shows a bump at ~142 that the model ignores while the baseline rides high). Candidate 1's linear baseline keeps peak areas physically meaningful. Although Candidate 1 uses more components (13) and more verification iterations, the extra components correspond to genuinely resolvable, physically expected features (doublets/splits), not noise-fitting, so the added complexity is justified.
